claim_as_stated: DAFpay default fee 2.9% rounded to whole dollars (a $25 gift pays ~4%); Bloomerang 4.85%, Donorbox 4.5% DAF fees.
exact_values_found: Chariot Nonprofit Terms (updated 2026-10-14): absent a platform agreement 'you will pay 2.9% (rounded to the nearest whole dollar) of the amount of any donation made through DAFpay'. $25 x 2.9% = $0.725 -> $1 = 4.0%. Givebutter help (2026-10-06): $500 gift -> $514.80 'rounded up to $515'. Bloomerang blog (modified 2026-10-29): 'Chariot charges 2.9% on DAF payments, and Bloomerang adds a 1.95% processing fee' = 4.85%. Donorbox: 1.6% platform + 2.9% Chariot = 4.5%. Chariot pricing page: 'Generally 2.9% fee'; DAFpay Components $199/mo + 2.9%.
discrepancies: None on numbers. A search-engine summary showed Bloomerang at 2.95% (=4.90%); the live page says 2.9%.
interpretation_challenge: 'Default' applies only where no platform agreement exists; most platforms let donors cover the fee, so the nonprofit's realised cost can be $0 and the fee then comes out of DAF assets. 4% at $25 depends on nearest-dollar rounding and is not documented as applied on every platform.

entity: DAF Direct; PayPal Giving Fund; Every.org
claim_as_stated: DAF Direct and PayPal Giving Fund charge nonprofits $0; Every.org For Good disbursement 1.5%.
source_date: live (footer (c)2013; lists DAFgiving360, so updated post-2023)
exact_values_found: DAF Direct: 'Neither you nor your donors will incur any download or transaction fees'; sponsors listed Fidelity Charitable, DAFgiving360, BNY Mellon Charitable. PayPal help: PPGF does not charge charities or donors fees (currency conversion may apply). Every.org pricing (search-index read; live page 429): Stripe weekly 0%, PayPal Grants 0%, For Good every 4-6 weeks 1.5%.
discrepancies: Every.org 1.5% not read from live page (HTTP 429); older Every.org help cites 2.25% (Network for Good era).
contradictory_evidence: A planned-giving site says DAF Direct integration carries 'a one-time small setup fee' (undated, unverified).
interpretation_challenge: PPGF $0 is to the charity but PPGF partner platforms may add fees; Every.org currently absorbs the For Good fee for bank-account donations and nonprofits avoid it by linking Stripe or PayPal Grants, so 1.5% is a worst-case, not typical, cost.

exact_values_found: Fidelity guide: statements, confirmations, tax receipts downloadable as PDFs; no CSV/Excel documented. No public Vanguard/NPT/GS/MS export documentation found in search. DAFgiving360 advisor (Schwab Advisor Center) grant-history 'Export' only via search summary.
discrepancies: Not independently refutable without logged-in access; absence in public material only.

interpretation_challenge: 'Publishes' is the operative word: logged-in exports may exist undocumented. Treat as 'no public documentation', not 'no export capability'.

claim_as_stated: SVCF's 2025 fund agreement prohibits automated data collection by donors/advisors.
exact_values_found: 'SVCF does not permit Fund Advisors, Secondary Advisors, or Fund Representatives ... to collect (through automated means or otherwise) any information from SVCF's website or donor portal ... for any purposes unrelated to the Authorized Advisor's grantmaking advisory privileges for their Fund.' 'THIRD-PARTY USE PROHIBITED: Only Fund Advisors and Secondary Advisors may make grant recommendations through the SVCF donor portal. Any access granted to a third party ... without SVCF's prior approval will be solely at the Authorized Advisor's risk' with indemnity.
discrepancies: The clause is purpose-limited, not a blanket ban: automated collection for the advisor's own grantmaking purposes is not prohibited by its text. The stronger restriction is on third-party portal access without prior approval (risk shifted to advisor plus indemnity).
interpretation_challenge: For agent access, the binding constraint is the third-party-use/indemnity clause, not the automated-collection clause.

entity: SVCF, GKCCF, San Diego Foundation, Omaha CF, Tulsa CF
claim_as_stated: SVCF, Greater Kansas City CF, San Diego Foundation, Omaha CF and Tulsa CF pay DAF grants by check.
exact_values_found: SVCF agreement: 'Grants made from funds at SVCF are generally issued by checks bearing the name and logo of SVCF'; SVCF handles payment '(e.g., check, wire, ACH, etc.)'. GKCCF: 'In most cases, a grant check from a fund at the Community Foundation will arrive in the mail from USPS' + sample grant check PDF (2024-11 upload). San Diego Foundation Recommend-a-Grant: 'Grant award checks are mailed directly to recipient nonprofit organizations' ((c)2026). Omaha CF How a Fund Works: 'checks to nonprofits are issued by the Foundation twice a week' ((c)2026). Tulsa CF Donor FAQ (2025-08): grant requests 'processed and mailed to the appropriate nonprofit agency'.
discrepancies: Tulsa is 'mailed' (check implied, not stated). SVCF and GKCCF say 'generally'/'in most cases', so electronic payment exists as an exception.
interpretation_challenge: 'Pay by check' should read 'pay by check by default/generally'; absence of a public ACH option is not proof none is offered on request.
